Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

precmed (development version)

Major changes

  • Added the population-level log.cumulative.hazard.ratio at tau0 to survival atefit(), with bootstrap inference. Inference is unavailable if the estimate or any bootstrap replicate is undefined. This replaces the conditional Cox log.hazard.ratio in atefit() output, a breaking change. Subgroup and validation conditional HR outputs remain available as hr.*; their values can change because of the horizon correction described below.

  • Added subgroup cumulative hazard ratios to survival catefit() and catecv() as chr.* outputs; hr.* outputs remain conditional Cox hazard ratios. Survival plots and box plots now accept measure = "rmtl" (default), "cumulative_hr", or "conditional_hr"; validation curves can display multiple measures. The previously supported plot.hr argument is deprecated; plot.hr = TRUE now selects the cumulative hazard ratio by default rather than the conditional Cox HR. Use measure = "conditional_hr" to plot the latter. Older saved objects must be refitted for cumulative hazard plots.

  • Added simulate_survival() to generate reproducible synthetic survival data illustrating confounding and heterogeneous treatment effects. Treatment, outcome, and censoring coefficients can be specified. The survival vignette now uses it; survivalExample remains available.

  • Added C backends, enabled by default, for count and survival contrast regression, Cox restricted mean survival integration, and LASSO propensity-score interaction screening. Installing from source now requires a C compiler and R’s standard BLAS/LAPACK libraries.

  • Added contrast.control, rmst.control, and ps.control for numerical backend settings. Set solver = "R" to use the R implementation; small floating-point differences between backends are possible.

  • Replaced gbm with gbm3 for boosting models. Existing tuning argument names and the learning rate of 0.1 are preserved; stored fits now have class GBMFit. Results can differ even with identical settings and random seeds.

  • Fixed continuous boosting predictions by retaining the selected tree count for each treatment arm, and forwarding additional boosting controls.

Minor changes and bug fixes

  • Validate outcome types and outcome-specific CATE scoring methods before fitting, including empty and invalid inputs.

  • Added catecvCountExample, a pre-fitted validation result used in the ABC and plotting examples to avoid repeatedly fitting models.

  • Label survival atefit() bootstrap plot panels with the original treatment names when available, and use readable names for the treatment effects.

  • Report automatic treatment recoding as an informational message rather than a warning, while retaining the mapping in existing result objects.

  • Added diagnostics() to summarize recorded survival atefit() treatment recoding information and subgroup errors and warnings from catefit() and catecv() results in a data frame.

  • Added coef() and confint() methods for extracting supported treatment effects and confidence intervals from count and survival atefit() results.

  • Fixed survival Cox hazard ratios to censor follow-up at tau0 instead of treating observations beyond the horizon as events. This affects subgroup and cross-validation hazard ratio estimates; this correction does not change the RMST and RMTL calculations.

  • Fixed survival random forest event coding at tau0 and integrated predicted survival curves through the full horizon when computing RMST. Survival forest scores and scores using forest initial predictions may change.

  • Warn when an out-of-range doubly robust RMST estimate is replaced by an outcome-model estimate, including when this occurs during bootstrap inference.

  • Fixed intercept-only propensity models in survival cross-fitting, subgroup evaluation, and bootstrap ATE estimation by preserving matrix dimensions.

  • Fixed LASSO propensity-score dimension handling with two predictors or a single prediction row.

  • Return NA with an informative warning for count-outcome responder subgroups missing one or both treatment arms, instead of failing the analysis. ABC is NA when a required validation estimate is unavailable.

  • Use GBM3 cross-validation for single-predictor count boosting fits and boosting initial predictions, removing the legacy out-of-bag workaround and fixing a cross-fitting error when selecting the number of trees.

  • Removed a duplicate treated-arm boosting fit in count cross-fitting. Results obtained with the same seed may change because fewer random draws are consumed.

  • Improved performance of balanced splitting, continuous contrast regression, censoring probability calculations, and propensity-score LASSO fitting.

  • Updated validation plots and box plots for current ggplot2 and tidyselect versions; ggplot2 >= 3.4.0 is now required.

  • Added the book chapter by Jiang et al. (2026) to the package description and references.

  • Added Smart Data Analysis and Statistics B.V. as copyright holder for its contributions after version 1.1.0, alongside the existing Biogen attribution.

precmed 1.1.0

CRAN release: 2024-10-05

  • Removed dependency on the MESS package.
  • Fixed an issue in the cross-validation procedure that lead to an increased total sample size
  • Updated documentation using roxygen2 (version 7.3.2) and resolved bracketing issues.

precmed 1.0.0.9000

  • Added a NEWS.md file to track changes to the package.
